notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP) succeeded fully; Shopify store. robots.txt explicitly Allow:/ for ClaudeBot, no opt-out. Pulled full /collections.json (311 collections across 2 pages) and grepped titles/handles for holiday keywords (Diwali, Christmas, Halloween, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi, Valentine, Eid, Thanksgiving, Easter, Mother's/Father's Day, Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, Onam, Pongal, festive/seasonal terms). No Halloween, Easter, Thanksgiving, Eid, Holi, Navratri, Onam, Pongal, or Ganesh-Chaturthi-branded collections exist anywhere in the taxonomy (confirmed absent, not just unsearched). Diwali was checked with particular care per instructions: found 4 Diwali-titled collections (Diwali Decorative Items, Diwali Candles Selection, Diwali Gift Ideas, Diwali Gifts for Family) plus a Lord Ganesha Statue collection. For every candidate collection, cross-checked the inflated /collections.json 'products_count' field against real /collections/<handle>/products.json enumeration (paginated to exhaustion, confirmed empty next page) per the qty-verification rule, and read the collection's own on-page description copy, and sampled/typed product titles (product_type + keyword match across the full product list) to test genuineness rather than trusting the title alone. This surfaced a clear pattern: several holiday-titled collections (Christmas Gifting, New Year Decor, Rakhi Gifting Guide, Secret Santa, Mother's Day Gifts, Mother's Day Gift Guide, Father's Day Gift Guide, Festive Collection 2023, Diwali Gift Ideas, and the broader Valentine Gifting) are large generic assortments spanning dozens of unrelated product types (photo frames, faux-leather trays, wine glasses, cushion covers, jewellery boxes, chess sets, bath towels, mirrors, etc.) with 0-1 holiday-keyword hits in product titles and heavy SKU overlap across DIFFERENT occasion collections (e.g. the same 'Set of 2 Clear Criss Cross Printed Wine Glasses' and 'Brown Croco Texture Faux Leather Pen Stand' appear in both the Rakhi and Father's Day collections) - these read as a shared generic 'small gift item' pool relabeled per occasion rather than genuine curated seasonal categories, functionally equivalent to the storewide-sale catch-all pattern the rules exclude, so they were excluded despite passing the surface title/description test. Mother's Day and Father's Day were evaluated on this same content basis (not reflexively excluded as 'universal gift occasions') and both failed: Mother's Day Gift Guide had only 1/227 titles with mom/mother keyword and the same generic product mix; Father's Day Gift Guide (31 items) was the same faux-leather-tray/photo-frame/wine-glass pattern seen in the excluded Rakhi and Mother's Day collections, just smaller. Lord Ganesha Statue (41 items, all genuinely Ganesha idols/figurines) was excluded because the site's own collection description frames it as a general everyday devotional/mandir decor item, not tied to Diwali or any specific festival in its copy - fails the 'site itself associates it with a holiday' test. Diwali Gifts for Family (0 products, unpublished in practice) excluded as empty. Included: (1) Diwali Decorative Items - explicit Diwali description copy ('Diwali is just round the corner... Diwali decoration items'), product mix concentrated in tealight/candle holders, hurricanes, torans, hanging garlands, decorative jars/bowls/vases (76/234 titles hit a diya/toran/lantern/tealight/candle/hurricane/garland keyword) - a genuine Diwali decor department. (2) Diwali Candles Selection - explicit Diwali candle-buying copy, 390 enumerated products, 13 product types, ~96% candles/diffusers/wax-filled-jars/tealight/pillar/votive/LED-candle SKUs - highly coherent. (3) Valentine Collection (handle valentineday-gifting) - explicit Valentine's Day copy, 148 enumerated products, 54/148 titles literally contain 'heart', and the remainder skew strongly to red/pink/rose color and rose-motif items (rose sprays, pink cushion covers, rose-berry candles) - a genuinely curated romantic/heart theme, distinct in character from the generic gifting collections. Qty for all 3 included rows is a verified full products.json enumeration (paginated with limit=250 until an empty page was returned), not the collections.json products_count field, since that field over-reported vs. the real product list for every collection checked (e.g. Diwali Decorative Items API field said 240 vs 234 real; Diwali Candles Selection said 405 vs 390 real; Valentine Collection said 162 vs 148 real).
